angles.cost_others: Going with the drift keeps things easy for everyone. Whenever you drift with a plan in place of saying what you wanted, you leave the people closest to you guessing. Remind yourself that you owe them a real answer, and the drift is not one.

angles.drive: Putting comfort ahead of the plan is how most evenings go. What you pour out all day leaves you emptier than you admit, so you take the comfort before anything is done. Do not forget that you enjoy comfort more once the thing is finished.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the day gets hard, you put comfort first and the hard part second. You comfort yourself rather than sit with it, while what you avoided waits for you unchanged. You are taking comfort where you needed rest, and tomorrow you are just as tired.
angles.cost_others: Keeping everyone around you comfortable comes before asking anything of them. Since you put a child's comfort ahead of what they promised, you take from them the small steadiness they needed. Remember that you get to be both the comforting one and the steady one.

angles.drive: What you have, you give away before checking whether enough is left. Since giving is the nearest you get to feeling like yourself, you give away more than you keep. You are one of the people you give to, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_self: Giving things away is quicker for you than working out what you need. Giving out more than comes back, you end most weeks with less than you started with. You go without exactly what you gave away, the rest and the money.
angles.cost_others: You give your hours to whoever is nearest, without deciding. Whenever you give everyone something rather than save enough for the few counting on you, you leave them less than was theirs. You give best from what you kept, and keeping is part of giving.

angles.drive: Your wit answers before your care does, and mostly you let it. Since being quick is how you know you are awake, you put the quick answer ahead of the careful one. Let the wit out, because you are kinder with it than you fear.
angles.cost_self: When talk gets hard, you reach the witty line before the honest one. You stay quick rather than get caught feeling something, until your wit lands where plain words belonged. Let plain words through, since each quick line costs you a piece of being known.
angles.cost_others: Saying the witty thing is how you take part. Getting the laugh with the quick line instead of letting one person finish, you cost them being heard out. Hold the wit while their point lands, because your timing is good enough to wait.

angles.drive: Doing a thing the usual way is nearly impossible for you, and only an original one feels done. Needing it in pieces first, you make your own version rather than follow the rule. Let originality count as talent, because it was never a fight.
angles.cost_self: Nothing feels real to you until you have made it original. You take being wrong your own way ahead of being right theirs, so you redo finished work. Count the originals that landed, with the rest paid for in hours you never owed.
angles.cost_others: Making an original version of what you were handed shows you cared. You make someone's plan your own instead of following it, and you deny them the small pride of a plan done as drawn. Carry one through unchanged sometimes, since your version can wait.

angles.drive: Not speaking up about something wrong is almost physically hard for you. You speak up ahead of being liked, because a true sentence left unsaid feels like a lie you took part in. Keep speaking up, since you are usually the only one who will.
angles.cost_self: Speaking up comes first, and counting the cost comes after. With honesty worth more to you than comfort, you speak up straight into fights you never meant to start. Leave one unsaid each month, because every unchosen fight costs you a friend's easy company.
angles.cost_others: When someone leaves a thing unsaid, you speak up about it as a kindness. Speaking up rather than waiting for them to work it out, you use up the time they needed. Ask first, since true and welcome are not the same gift.

angles.drive: What you think is already out loud, and the editing happens after. You have more Water than time to settle it, so you share the thought ahead of asking whether it is yours. Keep in mind that you choose what you share, true or not.
angles.cost_self: Sharing it all is easier than choosing which part, and you rarely choose. Since you let out more than comes back, you share every thought at full strength. You feel emptied afterwards, with nothing of it kept private.
angles.cost_others: To stay honest with people, you share everything you think. Sharing openly rather than asking what someone wants to hear, you take away their choice of how much to hold. You are allowed to let them ask before the rest comes out.

angles.drive: Mocking is your first language, and plain praise comes out like a foreign one. Since being clever feels safer than being seen caring, you mock what you love instead of praising it. Never forget that you mean the fondness more than the mocking lets on.
angles.cost_self: Where something matters to you, you mock it to keep it at a distance. You mock the thing you want instead of being seen wanting it, and the wish stays private. You already know the price, what you hoped for and never asked for straight.
angles.cost_others: You mock the people you are proudest of, because plain pride is too much. Sounding mocking rather than moved, you hand them praise with no way to keep it. Say the kind thing plainly, since the mocking is the part not worth keeping.

angles.drive: Picking a fight with a rule starts before you decide to. Since being told what to do feels like being made smaller, you pick the fight ahead of asking why. It is worth remembering that you pick the fight more often than it picks you.
angles.cost_self: Any push at all gets a fight out of you. You would rather lose on your terms than win on theirs, so you fight rules you never cared about. Skip the small fights, or each one you pick costs you a chance you wanted.
angles.cost_others: With whoever is in charge, you pick fights as your kind of honesty, audience included. Because you fight in public rather than private, you cost the one above you their footing in front of others. Pick the same fight in private first and lose nothing.

angles.drive: Your reach extends the way rivers extend, finding distant ground that stay-at-home currents never touch. The overseas client, the cousin of a stranger, the market two time zones away: your opportunities live at range, and distance has never once read as an obstacle to you.
angles.cost_self: The apartment in another country got rented through a chain of four people, none of whom you had met a year ago: a hostel conversation, a wedding, a group chat, a landlord. Your friends redraw the sequence on napkins and get lost. You just followed the water.
angles.cost_others: Your address book spans cities you have not visited yet, and somehow those entries pay off too. People far away describe you as the person to know locally, a math nobody can check. When anything needs to happen at distance, yours is the number that gets called.

angles.drive: You take the shape of whatever situation holds you, instantly and without losing yourself. The boardroom register, the market-stall banter, the funeral tone: each arrives on cue, native-sounding, no seams. Change of plans, change of country, change of fortune: you pour into the new container and proceed.
angles.cost_self: The flight got cancelled, the conference moved online, the currency dipped, and the deal closed anyway, renegotiated from a hotel lobby in a format invented that morning. Your colleague framed the itinerary as a souvenir of chaos. You framed the signed contract.
angles.cost_others: People stopped worrying about throwing you into new situations, since you land at operating temperature. New team, new city, new industry: within a month the locals assume you have always been there. The only constant across all your shapes, colleagues note, is the results.

angles.drive: Opportunity and company drift toward you the way streams find the low ground. You do not chase the introduction, the invitation, the tip: they arrive, carried by people who felt like telling you first. Something about your current makes things want to join it.
angles.cost_self: You sat alone at the airport bar for forty minutes and left with a job lead, a restaurant recommendation you later used, and the number of a supplier who now handles half your inventory. You had said maybe two hundred words. People just kept sitting down.
angles.cost_others: Hosts seat you strategically, having noticed the effect: conversation pools around your chair, introductions form near you unprompted, and the evening’s best story usually gets told in your direction. Networks assemble themselves around you while other people are still icebreaking.

angles.drive: Your fortunes rise and fall on currents you ride but never steer. The windfall month, the wipeout quarter, the rescue that arrives from nowhere, the loss that follows it out: your financial life reads like a tide chart with no moon to blame.
angles.cost_self: March brought the surprise contract that fixed everything, and August took it away with a client bankruptcy nobody saw coming. You have been rich twice and rinsed twice in four years, and your budgeting app has given up on trend lines. It just shows waves now.
angles.cost_others: People around you have stopped asking how business is going, because the answer has a tide in it. Family celebrates your peaks carefully, having attended the troughs. Somewhere in the up-and-down is an average that would support a calm life. Nobody, including you, has ever met it.

angles.drive: Nothing anchors. The city is temporary, the job is a stepping stone, the relationship is seeing where things go, and this has been true for eleven years. Your life is all current and no bed. Movement this constant looks free from the shore. From inside, lately, it just looks like water.
angles.cost_self: The storage unit in your old city still holds boxes from the move before last, paid monthly, visited never. Its contents would furnish the settled life you keep almost starting. The invoice arrives on the third of each month, a small bill for keeping every option open and none taken.
angles.cost_others: Old friends tell stories about you in the past tense while you are still alive and reachable, mostly because your presence never stays anywhere long enough for new chapters. You are missed in four cities, which sounds romantic. The visits stopped being planned around you years ago.

angles.drive: Your energy spreads across so many channels that no single one carries real depth. The five ventures, the three cities, the dozen half-relationships: everything gets a trickle, and trickles evaporate. The delta looks impressive from above. At ground level, none of the streams can float a boat.
angles.cost_self: Tuesday touched four projects in three currencies and finished none of anything. The calls overlapped, the follow-ups queued, and at midnight you were answering messages for the venture that earns the least, because it shouts the loudest. The one that could actually flourish got eleven minutes.
angles.cost_others: Partners in each of your streams believe they have a quarter of you, and the math says less. They compare schedules sometimes, your various people, and find the sum does not close. Everything you touch stays alive and nothing thrives, and everyone waits for a consolidation the current keeps postponing.

angles.drive: You handle resources the way careful water handles a landscape, never taking more than the channel can hold. The purchase gets slept on, the debt gets declined, the plan keeps a margin. Boring, people say, until their own accounts get interesting in the bad way.
angles.cost_self: The car was chosen after the insurance quote, the reliability data, and one conversation with a mechanic you trust. It has now outlasted three of your friends’ flashier choices, at half the total cost. The spreadsheet that picked it is still on your laptop, mildly famous.
angles.cost_others: Friends consult you before their big decisions the way travelers check the depth of a river before driving in. Your questions are unexciting and save fortunes: what does it cost per year, what happens if it breaks. Several disasters in your circle simply never happened. That was you.

angles.drive: Your resources move like a reliable stream, in on schedule, out with intention, never flash-flooding. The salary lands, the transfers fire, the obligations get met a little early. Drama has no purchase on your finances, and the calm compounds as quietly as the interest.
angles.cost_self: Rent has arrived on the first for eleven consecutive years, across three landlords, one recession, and a broken leg. The current landlord once called to check the transfer was real, so rare is the species. You are the tenant reference other applicants wish existed.
angles.cost_others: The people downstream of you, family, dependents, one perpetually struggling friend, plan their lives around a reliability they have stopped noticing. The support just arrives, monthly, like weather in a fortunate climate. Nobody asks what maintaining a stream that steady requires. It requires everything, daily.

angles.drive: The future finds you already provisioned. The renewal date is in the calendar, the emergency fund holds six months, the umbrella lives in the car. Your readiness is so habitual it looks like luck: things simply never seem to catch you without the relevant item.
angles.cost_self: When the layoffs came, your household absorbed the news with a strange calm: the fund was there, the resume was current, the numbers had been run in advance during a peaceful January. The panic that visited every other affected house found yours already interviewed and hired.
angles.cost_others: People tease the preparations right up until they need them, at which point you become briefly, intensely popular. The jump cables, the spare charger, the printed copy: someone borrows one weekly. You have become the reason other people can afford to be spontaneous. Nobody sends a card.

angles.drive: Your resources pool behind walls you keep raising. The money accumulates and does not move, the generosity is rationed through a narrow spillway, and downstream, things that needed watering are visibly dry. The reservoir is impressive. Reservoirs, unvisited, are just deep places holding still.
angles.cost_self: The account crossed the threshold you once named as enough, and the threshold moved the same week, upward, as it always moves. Your niece’s tuition request took three weeks to answer and came back a loan, papered, at interest. Family dinners since have had a different acoustics.
angles.cost_others: People stopped asking, which you registered as peace. The requests dried up, the little fundraisers route around you, and the reputation settled like silt: comfortable, careful, closed. The wealth is real and growing. What it is for remains, to everyone including you, the open question.

angles.drive: Every offer arrives at your door pre-suspected. The deal has a catch, the kindness has an angle, the stranger has a reason: your default read is downstream contamination, and proof of purity is a standard almost nothing meets. You are rarely cheated. You are also rarely surprised by joy.
angles.cost_self: The neighbor’s offer to water your plants during your trip triggered a full risk assessment: motive, key custody, precedent. You declined with thanks and paid a service. The plants did fine. The neighbor waved differently afterward, from slightly further away, permanently.
angles.cost_others: People approach you with their cards face up and their movements slow, having learned that anything else reads as an angle. The honest ones find the screening mildly insulting and mostly stop volunteering. What gets through your filter is genuinely safe. So little gets through.

angles.drive: Letting go, of money, of objects, of the way Sunday is supposed to run, activates something in your grip that logic cannot pry open. The sunk cost stays sunk and held, the worn-out thing stays shelved, and your hands, at any given moment, are completely full.
angles.cost_self: The vacation fund has existed for nine years and never once been spent, each proposed trip failing the final review at the moment of booking. The money is for vacations. The vacations are somehow never quite worth the money. The fund grows, a monument to trips unrisked.
angles.cost_others: Prying anything from you, a concession, an old coat for the charity bag, an admission that plans changed, has a known difficulty rating among your people. They mostly stopped trying and started working around the grip. Your hands hold everything. Notably, lately, that includes very little of theirs.

angles.drive: Your temperature drops as situations heat up, which is backwards from most people and priceless in a crisis. The angrier the meeting, the clearer your sentences get. Decisions made in your coolness hold up later, when everyone rereads what the heat almost signed.
angles.cost_self: Both founders were shouting by the time you spoke, and your first sentence was a number. Your second was a date. The shouting had nowhere to attach itself to numbers, and the meeting ended with a plan bearing your fingerprints and their signatures.
angles.cost_others: Opponents find your calm the most alarming thing in the fight. While they heat up, you cool down, and every degree they rise hands you another advantage. Beating you requires making you blink first. The people who have tried compare notes afterward, uselessly.

angles.drive: You look directly at what others manage around. The bad diagnosis, the failing numbers, the conversation everyone keeps rescheduling: your gaze goes straight in, takes the true measure, and does not flinch on contact. Reality respects you for it and returns the favor with early warnings.
angles.cost_self: When the project was dying, you were the one who said dying, out loud, in week two instead of month four. The word landed like cold water. It also saved the quarter, because everything that followed was built on the actual situation instead of the brochure.
angles.cost_others: People borrow your eyes for their hardest looks: the contract they are afraid to reread, the feedback they suspect is true, the mole on the shoulder. You never soften the report and never sharpen it either. Afterward they know, which was the entire point.

angles.drive: When you move, it lands where it matters, at depth. No warning shots, no surface noise: you wait, read the current, and place one action where the whole structure turns. People rarely see your strike. They see everything afterward arranging itself differently.
angles.cost_self: You said nothing in three consecutive negotiations, then made one call to one person on a Thursday, and the entire deal reorganized around it by Monday. Colleagues spent the week reconstructing what happened. What happened was patience with coordinates.
angles.cost_others: Rivals underestimate you at intake because you make no ripples, and revise their opinion exactly once. The revision is permanent. Around your industry there is a small collection of stories that all end the same way: nobody saw it coming, and it only needed to come once.

angles.drive: Your displeasure arrives as temperature. There is never a scene: the warmth simply leaves the water, and everyone in it notices at once. People can handle anger. The cold is harder, because there is nothing to answer and nowhere to warm up.
angles.cost_self: You said nothing wrong at dinner. You said almost nothing at all, and the table spent two hours in a careful climate, passing dishes with light hands. Your partner asked afterward what happened. Nothing happened, you said, at a temperature that confirmed everything.
angles.cost_others: People describe crossing you with weather words: frost, freeze, ice age. The thaw comes eventually, unannounced, and everyone pretends the winter did not happen. But they dress for it now, permanently, and some conversations never come back indoors.

angles.drive: Once you commit to pressure, it does not stop. The follow-up, the reminder, the revisited grievance: your current keeps flowing against the same rock long after the point was made, and past where the point began eroding the ground it stood on.
angles.cost_self: The dispute with the contractor was won in March, with a refund and an apology. You were still composing documentation in June. The folder is spotless and the war is over, and only one side has noticed the second fact.
angles.cost_others: People settle with you early because they have seen what the long version costs. Your persistence wins real victories, and it has also outlived several relationships that surrendered years before you stopped. The current cannot tell the difference between resistance and rubble.

angles.drive: Your force pulls downward quietly. Deadlines, standards, and consequences settle over people like water over a diver, heavier with every meter, and nobody can point to the moment breathing got hard. You never raise your voice. The pressure does the talking, at depth.
angles.cost_self: The new hire was excellent for three months, then quieter, then gone, and the exit interview mentioned an atmosphere no single incident could explain. You reread it twice, genuinely puzzled. Each individual expectation had been reasonable. Together they were an ocean on someone’s chest.
angles.cost_others: Teams under you produce and pale at the same time, and the best people leave while thanking you sincerely. From your seat it looks like standards working. From theirs it was the slow discovery of how deep the water had gotten while they were busy swimming.

angles.drive: Your discipline flows in built channels: the routine, the process, the documented way. Where others improvise and flood, you move the same water through the same course daily, and things downstream can rely on it. Order, in your hands, is irrigation rather than dam.
angles.cost_self: The morning sequence has not changed in nine years: the walk, the list, the first hard task before mail. Colleagues set meetings around it like farmers around rainfall. On the rare day the sequence breaks, three people ask if everything is alright. It usually is, by ten.
angles.cost_others: Systems you build keep working after you leave them, which people discover with surprise and gratitude. The handover document from your last role is still in use, word for word, four successors later. Somebody described inheriting your process as moving into a house with the plumbing already perfect.

angles.drive: You hold your shape under pressure the way deep water holds its level: visibly, reassuringly, without effort you would admit to. The difficult meeting, the public mistake, the audit: your surface stays level, and everyone in the region borrows a little of it.
angles.cost_self: When your name was mentioned unfairly in the all-hands, forty faces turned to watch yours. It gave them nothing: a nod, a note taken, a follow-up requested calmly afterward through channels. The retraction came within the week, and your pulse, whatever it did, did it privately.
angles.cost_others: People bring you bad news first, specifically, because your reaction never adds to the problem. The messengers relax mid-sentence, watching it land in still water. What it costs you to keep the surface level is a figure nobody has ever seen, which is the point of paying it.

angles.drive: You plan at distances other people reserve for fantasy. The pension started at twenty-three, the succession question asked a decade early, the consequence spotted three moves before it forms. Present-tense people find it eerie. Future-tense people find it, eventually, in their interest.
angles.cost_self: The clause you insisted on in 2019, the one everyone called paranoid, activated last spring and saved the partnership six figures. You accepted the apologies without ceremony. The next contract contains four such clauses. Nobody calls them paranoid now. They call them yours.
angles.cost_others: People check plans against your horizon the way ships check charts, especially for the waters nobody has entered yet. Your predictions are unglamorous and mostly correct, delivered early enough to act on. The ones who listened compound the benefit. The ones who did not become examples.

angles.drive: Every risk gets weighed until it drowns. The checking, the double-checking, the waiting for conditions: your prudence has a thoroughness that outlives most opportunities. Nothing bad happens to you, statistically. The cost is that remarkably little of anything happens, and the ledger never shows it.
angles.cost_self: The investment you researched for six months appreciated forty percent while the research matured. You printed the analysis anyway, complete and correct, a beautiful audit of a ship that had sailed. It sits in the drawer with its siblings. The drawer is thick with correct conclusions.
angles.cost_others: People stopped waiting for your green light years ago, since it arrives after the intersection has cleared. They proceed, and you catch up, cautiously, once the road is proven. Your record contains no disasters and no adventures, and only one of those absences was chosen.

angles.drive: Your voice arrives pre-softened, and the softening costs content. The objection becomes a question, the question becomes a pause, the pause gets read as agreement. What you actually think is audible only at very close range, and most decisions get made from further away.
angles.cost_self: You disagreed with the plan in the meeting where it could have mattered, silently, and again in the hallway, quietly, to someone with no vote. The plan proceeded and failed roughly as you had predicted. Your prediction exists in no record. It was a very correct whisper.
angles.cost_others: Colleagues dig up your opinions years later, over drinks: you had doubts about that? The doubts were real and beautifully reasoned and entirely internal. People would have listened, they insist. You nod, unconvinced, quietly, which is of course the whole mechanism in miniature.

angles.drive: The channel decides your route. The established procedure, the way it has always flowed, the course set by someone upstream years ago: you follow it faithfully, even where the banks have visibly moved. Freedom to reroute exists on paper. The water has never once tested it.
angles.cost_self: The weekly report you compile takes three hours and, as of the reorg two years ago, has no remaining readers. You suspected as much and confirmed it once, gently, then continued compiling. The channel was dug and the water flows. Somewhere that is still a reason.
angles.cost_others: People watch you execute obsolete instructions with a loyalty that would be moving on a battlefield and is puzzling in an office. New options get presented to you and acknowledged and left on the bank. The current knows one direction. Everyone has stopped suggesting there are others.

angles.drive: Going deep is the only way you learn. Half-knowing bothers you more than not knowing at all, so you follow one question down until the floor shows. You pay for the one you own with every subject left at the surface.
angles.cost_self: Where you go deepest is where you are most at home. You would rather stay down with one question than come up for the people and chances passing overhead. You lose nothing of the depth by surfacing a little sooner, and keep the open door.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you go deep, you go alone. Company slows you down, and you pick the quiet ahead of any company you did not choose. Once in a while take someone down with you instead of handing them the summary.

angles.drive: You read what a person is not saying. A pause tells you more than the words around it, so you trust your feeling about someone ahead of the story you are given. Say the reading out loud, because an unsaid one cannot be corrected.
angles.cost_self: Reading a person ahead of their words keeps you from surprises. The reading comes faster than the asking, and you go with it instead of waiting for the rest. Ask the slow question anyway, because the closeness you skip is what being right early costs.
angles.cost_others: Where someone stops short, you read the rest and answer it. Reading them feels like care, and you answer the unsaid rather than wait to be told it. You give the other person back their telling whenever you let the sentence finish.

angles.drive: You teach yourself what matters most to you. A lesson you worked out alone sits deeper than one handed to you, and your own odd route comes ahead of the course on offer. You lose years to the long way and would take it again.
angles.cost_self: Teaching yourself spares you being a beginner anywhere. Working it out alone feels easier than asking someone who knows, and the long road is the one you choose. Ask sooner than you want to, because the help you refuse gets paid for in years.
angles.cost_others: You taught yourself your own route, and it is hard to pass on. Showing the steps means admitting there were none, and you hand over the answer rather than the method. Write the route down, because the way is what anyone learning from you misses.

angles.drive: You think a decision over long after it stopped needing thought. Water comes into you faster than you spend it, and one more angle feels like care rather than delay. You know by now that you only learn from the choices you make.
angles.cost_self: Thinking too much is your way of not being wrong. A wrong call scares you more than a late one, so you think a choice over past its day. Keep in mind that you lose chances this way without a sound, and sleep with them.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone needs an answer, you think it over once more. Getting it right matters more to you than getting it to them, and you hand over the wait. It is worth remembering that you give more by replying now than by replying right.

angles.drive: You keep what you know in until it is finished, and it never is. More goes into you than comes out, because a half-formed thought let loose feels like a thought lost. Remember that you would rather keep an idea safe than see it used.
angles.cost_self: Keeping it in keeps it from being judged. Inside is where an idea stays safe, so you hold yours back until perfect rather than let it out rough. Do not forget that you lose the chance to be heard while waiting to be ready.
angles.cost_others: You keep in what others could use. A thought let out early feels broken to you, so you hold it in rather than hand it over. Remember how much more you help with half an answer than with a whole one never said.

angles.drive: You are hard to reach even from across the table. Most of you lives in an unfinished thought, and you would rather finish it than answer the person in front of you. Remember you are only as reachable as the part that surfaces.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to reach keeps your thinking whole. An interruption costs you the thread, so you answer late or not at all rather than lose it. You already know that you trade closeness for that thread, and closeness does not wait.
angles.cost_others: Hard to reach means a thought is unfinished, and most of yours are. Finishing it comes ahead of the message, and you charge the person waiting in days. Remind yourself that you are worth more fully there than mostly away.

angles.drive: You calm people down without trying to. Taking in someone's worry costs you less than watching them carry it, so you take it in and give back something steadier. Let a little of it out somewhere, because calm you only absorb runs dry.
angles.cost_self: Being the calm one is a job you never put down. You take in other people's upset and level it, while yours waits for a quiet that never comes. You leave your own upset unsettled until you let someone steady you for once.
angles.cost_others: When someone close to you is upset, you become the calm for both. Being needed suits you more than being known, and your own trouble never shows. Let them see you shaken sometimes, because calm with nothing behind it keeps people at a distance.

angles.drive: You soak things up rather than study them. It settles into you from whatever is nearby, so you know a thing long before you can pass a test on it. You can trust the gap, since the proof turns up later than the understanding.
angles.cost_self: Soaking it up is how learning stays with you. Sitting with it until it is yours comes easier than proving it on paper, and the proof is the part you skip. Get the paper once, because the chances asking for it close without you.
angles.cost_others: Soaking up what someone says comes ahead of deciding whether you agree. Taking it in is easier than pushing back, so your disagreement stays where it helps no one. You help more with an honest no than a kind yes, and yours is already there.

angles.drive: Being patient comes easily to you. Letting a thing come in its own time feels more honest than forcing it, and you can wait on a question for months. Keep your pace, because the price is only the chance that needed a push.
angles.cost_self: Being patient also means you never have to ask. Waiting for a thing to come to you feels easier than reaching, so the wanting stays quiet until the chance passes. You gave up what you never asked for without noticing, and one question changes that.
angles.cost_others: You wait for a person to be ready rather than hurry them toward it. Not hurrying feels like respect, and you let someone stay stuck longer than kindness needed. Push sometimes, because being patient is also the hand you kept back.

angles.drive: You let things drift rather than decide them, and you call it patience. There is more Water in you than you turn into motion, so choosing costs more than going along. Remember that when you drift you are choosing too, just not the outcome.
angles.cost_self: Drifting keeps the days quiet, and quiet feels like care. Stirring nothing costs less than reaching, and you renew the lease rather than ask what you want. Do not lose sight of how little you learn of your own wants while nothing changes at home.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you let drift, you leave to someone else. Being carried feels easier than steering, and you let the people close to you make the calls you never did. It helps to remember that you hand them the weight of every call you dodge.

angles.drive: You stay where it is safe long after outgrowing it. Shelter is the thing you trust most, so you pick the known ahead of the better whenever the two come apart. Remember that you keep the shelter even after you walk out of it.
angles.cost_self: Staying in is how you avoid being tested. Not being ready feels more honest than being ready, and you stay long past the day leaving was open to you. Never forget that you give up the very chances the shelter was for by staying in.
angles.cost_others: Staying sheltered keeps you home while others go out. You pick being safe ahead of being there, and watch the invitations thin out instead of going. You hand those you love your safety in place of your company, and the swap is yours to notice.

angles.drive: You over-protect the people you love from what they could survive. Watching someone struggle hurts you more than doing it for them, so the help comes before the asking. Keep in mind how completely you can protect someone, until not even the lesson reaches them.
angles.cost_self: Over-protecting the ones you love never rests. Taking the hit for someone is easier for you than watching them take it, so you carry what was never yours. Bear in mind what you pay in rest for every hit you absorb for another person.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone you love is about to struggle, you over-protect and step in first. Sparing them the hard part feels like love, and you choose their comfort rather than their growing. Remember that you take from them the one lesson that would have stuck.

angles.drive: Your fire needs no external ignition. Motivation, celebration, recovery: all generated onboard, on your schedule, from your own fuel. Gray seasons that dim everyone else find your output unchanged, and people eventually ask where the switch is. There is no switch. There is just you, on.
angles.cost_self: The whole team went flat after the funding fell through, and you came in Monday running on the same setting as always, working the plan, playing your music. By Wednesday two others had re-lit off your example. Nobody discussed it. Flame transfers that way, wordlessly.
angles.cost_others: People keep expecting your energy to trace back to something: the routine, the diet, the secret. They audit your habits and find nothing transferable. The light is simply factory-installed, and the people who winter near you have learned to stop explaining it and start standing closer.

angles.drive: You are unmistakably yourself at all times, and it costs you nothing. The opinions, the laugh, the orange shirt: none of it adjusts to the audience, because none of it was built for an audience. People meet one version of you. There is only one.
angles.cost_self: At the new job you dressed, joked, and disagreed exactly as you had at the old one, from day one. No feeling-out period, no beige phase. Within a month the team could imitate you affectionately, which is what happens to people who are only themselves.
angles.cost_others: Nobody has ever described you as an acquired taste, because there is nothing gradual about you. People place you instantly and permanently. Years later, strangers from one meeting recall you in detail, while the adaptable people around you have blurred together in everyone’s memory.

angles.drive: Setbacks that lower other people’s flames leave your wattage stubbornly constant. The rejection, the rough year, the public stumble: each arrives expecting to find a dimmer switch and finds instead a person already back at brightness, slightly annoyed at the interruption.
angles.cost_self: The restaurant failed in March, publicly, expensively, and by June you were catering weddings out of a rented kitchen with the same menu and better margins. People kept waiting for the humbled chapter. You skipped it, apparently unaware it was scheduled, and the food got better.
angles.cost_others: People measure resilience against you and quietly retire the word for themselves. Your relights after failure have become local legend: same heat, new venue, no visible scar tissue. Investors who lost money on your last thing keep asking about your next one. Light like yours audits well.

angles.drive: Your flame refuses to be seen flickering. The struggle stays private, the help gets declined at the door, the apology exits in a dialect nobody recognizes as one. Being impressive is mandatory, being witnessed mid-failure is not survivable, and the policy costs you exactly what it protects.
angles.cost_self: The business wobbled for five months before anyone knew, because the version of you at dinners kept performing success on schedule. When the closure finally announced itself, friends were hurt in an unexpected direction: you had let them toast a ghost. The pride had spent their trust.
angles.cost_others: People edit their offers of help into compliments before approaching you, a translation service everyone runs and nobody acknowledges. Your worst seasons are visible only in hindsight, dated by gaps in the photo record. The support you never requested was available the whole time, warming nobody.

angles.drive: Being treated as less than an equal lights you up faster than any insult. The talked-over sentence, the credit handed elsewhere, the tone that files you under junior: your heat answers before your judgment gets a vote. The issue is never the thing. It is the standing.
angles.cost_self: The contractor explained your own trade to you, slowly, and the meeting changed temperature. You corrected him once, precisely, at volume. He was right about one small detail and never got to say it, which cost you a week and won you nothing.
angles.cost_others: People around you learn the one rule quickly: never talk down to you, even by accident. Introductions get made carefully, titles included. The respect this enforces is real, and so is the caution, and the two arrive together, holding hands.

angles.drive: Your brightness reads as a closed door. The confidence, the speed, the shine: together they build a glare people squint at from a distance, assuming you need nothing and no one. Invitations to depth stopped arriving years ago. Everyone assumed someone else was providing it.
angles.cost_self: At your lowest week in years, the phone stayed silent, and you realized the silence was your own engineering: a decade of seeming complete had trained everyone out of checking. The one friend who did call apologized twice for intruding. You were, you said brightly, fine.
angles.cost_others: New people orbit you at a fixed radius, warmed but not close, sensing no docking port in all that light. The intimates you do have all report the same onboarding: years of proximity before the first real conversation. Most people, understandably, settle for the glow and drift.

angles.drive: You run toward whatever is catching fire, and the running is the point. The contested deal, the live crisis, the dare with witnesses: your blood answers heat the way others answer comfort. In a world of careful people, you are the one already moving, already lit.
angles.cost_self: When the flagship store’s launch collapsed at noon, you drove there without being asked, arriving mid-panic with energy the situation had run out of. By close, the day was saved and slightly legendary. Your boss asked who sent you. Nobody had. The smoke had.
angles.cost_others: Teams keep you near the volatile accounts the way stations keep engines running. When something flares, you are moving before the call finishes, and colleagues have learned to just hand you the keys. The calm assignments bore you visibly. Nobody wastes you on them anymore.

angles.drive: Your asks have no ceiling. The cold call to the CEO, the bid above your class, the public promise that forces the miracle: you say the enormous thing out loud, and enough of it lands to fund the reputation. Fortune does seem to favor you. You invoice it accordingly.
angles.cost_self: You pitched the biggest client in the region from the lobby, uninvited, with a deck finished that morning in the car. Security was called and, in the end, so was the account manager. The contract took eight months. The story reached your industry in eight days.
angles.cost_others: People preface their descriptions of you with you will not believe, and the stories hold up under checking. Some rivals call the boldness reckless from a safe distance. Your collaborators call it Tuesday, and have learned to draft the press release before you finish the sentence.

angles.drive: Your energy transfers on contact. The flat team meeting catches current when you enter, the tired project finds voltage, the gathering’s pulse syncs upward to yours. People leave your orbit doing things they had filed under someday. The battery, mysteriously, never bills anyone.
angles.cost_self: The fundraiser was dying at forty percent with a week left, and your two-day blitz of calls, stunts, and shameless enthusiasm dragged it to one-forty. Volunteers who had gone quiet came back loud. The organizer’s thank-you note said simply: you plugged us back in.
angles.cost_others: People describe meetings before and after your arrival as different weather. Managers deploy you into stalled teams the way medics deploy adrenaline, and the effect is roughly as fast. The crash that sometimes follows is also documented. Everyone considers it worth it, and schedules for it.

angles.drive: The fuse is short, dry, and pre-lit. The wrong word, the cut-off in traffic, the tone in an email: ignition beats deliberation to the scene every time. Afterward you cool fast and repair sincerely. The people nearby, though, have all learned the smell of smoke.
angles.cost_self: The referee’s call was wrong, and your response, at a children’s game, entered neighborhood folklore within the hour. You apologized to everyone by sundown, sincerely, including the referee. Your daughter accepted the apology and, the following week, asked you to wait in the car.
angles.cost_others: People manage your temperature the way sound engineers manage feedback, adjusting topics before the squeal. Certain news gets delivered to you in public places, on purpose. You noticed the pattern once and got angry about it, which, everyone agreed silently, rather settled the question.

angles.drive: Other people’s wins sit on your skin like sunburn. The peer’s promotion, the friend’s effortless luck, the rival’s applause: each one stings out of proportion, and the sting talks. It comes out as jokes with edges and praise with subtitles. Everyone reads the subtitles.
angles.cost_self: At the launch party for your friend’s startup, funded on the first try, your toast included the phrase must be nice twice, laughed off both times, remembered anyway. The friendship survived. Its temperature dropped four degrees that night and never fully came back to season.
angles.cost_others: Your congratulations arrive with a delay everyone has learned to expect, like sound after lightning. People soft-launch their successes around you, understating, apologizing for luck. They do it out of care, which would wound you worst of all, so it stays carefully unmentioned.

angles.drive: Pressure in you does not vent. It stores, silently, behind a warm exterior, until the container fails all at once. The blowups arrive without visible warning, sized for the backlog rather than the trigger, and the cleanup involves people who never saw the gauge climbing.
angles.cost_self: The garage door sticking was the trigger, but the detonation covered March through August: the job, the loan, the unsaid things, all of it airborne in one four-minute burst. Your family stood very still. The door, notably, still sticks. Nobody mentions it now.
angles.cost_others: People close to you have become seismologists, reading your quiet for pressure signs and mostly getting it wrong, because the gauge is internal and you politely deny it exists. The denials are calm right up until they are not. Afterward everyone, including you, surveys the range.

angles.drive: Giving is the easiest thing you do. You would rather be useful than be thanked, and you give ahead of being asked. Keep giving this freely, and notice its one price, the flat hour when nothing is needed from you.
angles.cost_self: Something to give away is where you are most at ease. Giving comes before wanting, and you would sooner give one more thing than name what you need. Take a turn too, because your enjoyment is the gift you keep skipping.
angles.cost_others: Whenever the people around you need something, you have given it before they ask. Providing feels safer than receiving, so you hand out more than you let in. Let them give back sometimes, because you have been taking that chance from them.

angles.drive: Enjoying something quietly was never your way. You feel a pleasure fully only once it is shared, and you would rather enjoy a small thing with company than a big thing alone. You pay for enjoying out loud with the private kind, a fair trade.
angles.cost_self: Enjoyment only counts for you when it is shared. You write off an evening alone as wasted, and you pick less enjoyment in company ahead of more by yourself. Learn to enjoy the quiet kind too, because the rest in it is yours to keep.
angles.cost_others: Whatever you enjoy, you pull the people near you into enjoying as well. You run the fun rather than have it, and you leave little for the quieter people to add. Leave some open, because you take the air their smaller pleasures need.

angles.drive: What you make comes out without strain. Ease is the sign you trust, and you do the thing that flows sooner than you force the thing that counts. If it came without effort, you own it a little less, and that is the whole price.
angles.cost_self: Effort was never your measure of worth. You rate what comes easily below what you fought for, so you hand the easy work over free ahead of charging for it. Price the ease too, because the money you wave off is the cost.
angles.cost_others: You make hard things look easy. You show the finished thing sooner than the work, and you leave the people learning from you the ease without the steps. Work at something in front of them once, since you teach more by steps than by ease.

angles.drive: Saying no has never come easily to you. Helping feels more like you than resting does, and you say yes ahead of checking the cost. Remember that every yes comes out of you, and less goes back in.
angles.cost_self: Staying on good terms with whoever asks is what your yes is for. Being needed feels safer than being rested, so you say yes to the evening rather than keep it. Do not forget that you pay for each refused rest with your health.
angles.cost_others: You answer whoever asks first with a yes, and you leave the people at home what is left. Pleasing the person in front of you comes ahead of keeping your word at home. Bear in mind, you owe them the follow-through more than the yes.

angles.drive: You drift toward whatever asks the least of you. You treat comfort as the reward you are owed, and you let a day drift rather than steer it. Worth remembering that you are drifting in a direction too, only not one you picked.
angles.cost_self: Drifting costs you nothing on any single day. Taking it easy feels better than taking it on, so you put off the thing you meant to make again. Look again at the one thing you most wanted to make, because you keep drifting past it.
angles.cost_others: Whatever the people around you decide, you drift along with it. Going along feels better than having a view, and you hand the deciding to whoever is nearest. Try to remember that you leave them carrying choices you were meant to share.

angles.drive: You put pleasure first and the rest after. Feeling good is how you check you are alive, so you take the nicer option ahead of the needed one. Keep hold of this, that you run the pleasure on yourself and it puts nothing back.
angles.cost_self: Pleasure first is the one care you trust. Feeling comforted matters more to you than feeling well, and you take comfort now ahead of health later. You pay for it in the body, and the body keeps a longer memory than you do.
angles.cost_others: Whenever a plan with others meets your pleasure, you choose the pleasure. You take a good time now sooner than a promise kept later, and you spend the house money on the evening. Remember whose share you are spending, since part of it is theirs.

angles.drive: You speak up right where it has gone quiet. You hear silence as agreeing, and you say the unsaid thing rather than sit with it. Keep speaking up, and own its price, since you are remembered for the sentence more than the care behind it.
angles.cost_self: Speaking up is the part of you that never needs rehearsing. You find the clever answer faster than the careful one, and you say it ahead of checking the cost. You close a chance you wanted with a good line more often than you notice.
angles.cost_others: Before anyone asks you to, you speak up for them. Having a voice comes more naturally to you than lending one, so you take the floor ahead of handing it over. Leave the quieter ones the first word, because you speak up on their turn.

angles.drive: You change in front of an audience, for the better. Being watched is where your focus comes from, and you perform a thing sooner than you practice it. You pay for that in private, since nothing you do alone feels quite finished.
angles.cost_self: Performing is how you make things count. Being seen doing it matters more to you than doing it, so you keep performing after the show ends. Give yourself an hour with no one watching, because the rest you skip is the price of the stage.
angles.cost_others: For the people you love, you perform as much as for a crowd. Company feels like a show to you, and your best lines come ahead of your plain self. Save them one plain evening, because you keep performing where you were asked for yourself.

angles.drive: You think fastest with no time to think. You light up under pressure rather than freeze, so you answer on the spot instead of taking it away with you. You rarely give the slow answer its turn, and the speed is worth that most days.
angles.cost_self: Thinking fast is the talent you lean on hardest. You have the first answer before the question is finished, and you trust it ahead of the second. You spend the better answer you never waited for to keep the quickness.
angles.cost_others: Fast enough to finish other people's sentences, you usually do. Waiting for a thought to end feels like wasted time, and you answer ahead of hearing it all. Let the slow thought finish, because you cost the slower ones the rest of theirs.

angles.drive: Talking back comes faster to you than letting it pass. Being told what to do feels like shrinking, and you talk back rather than let a rule stand. Remember that each answer is drawn from you, and you put in less than you spend.
angles.cost_self: Getting pushed around is what talking back saves you from. Being right out loud counts for more with you than being kept on, and you say the thing that ends the conversation. Worth remembering, you talk yourself out of the chances you wanted most.
angles.cost_others: You talk back to whoever asks something of you before the ask is done. You hear a request as a demand, and you answer the tone ahead of the need. Notice how you leave them holding a fight they never brought.

angles.drive: You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, and you take being watched doing badly over doing well alone. Hold onto this, that you are the one left when the audience goes home.
angles.cost_self: Without an audience, you will not start. Practicing alone feels like wasted effort, and you save the real work for a crowd rather than do it unseen. Never forget that you starve the talent between shows, and between shows is where it grows.
angles.cost_others: What you need from the people close to you is watching more than joining in. You feel company only once it is facing you, and you turn a friend into a crowd. Remember, you take their evening and hand back a show.

angles.drive: You overdo it, and you know it while you do. You never feel enough as a real amount, so you push a thing past its best rather than stop there. Mind that you run out well before the thing does.
angles.cost_self: Overdoing it is how you get a thing noticed. You feel safer with more than with enough, and you give a small occasion the full show. You pay with the body for each full show, and the bill never fails to arrive after the applause.
angles.cost_others: For people who asked for little, you overdo it anyway. You feel a plain yes as too little, so you hand them the full production instead of what they named. Keep track of the extra you leave them to carry beyond what was asked.

angles.drive: You see the catch of an opportunity before there is visible flame. The undervalued block, the platform before the crowd, the person about to become somebody: your eye finds the ember while everyone else needs the bonfire. Being early is your entire portfolio, and it keeps paying.
angles.cost_self: You bought the ugly little stand at the market’s dead corner because the foot traffic map in your head disagreed with the rent. Two seasons later the corner was the market, and the rent conversation went differently, in your favor, with you on the landlord side.
angles.cost_others: Friends have learned to note what you mention twice, since your casual enthusiasms have a habit of becoming everyone’s expensive enthusiasms two years later. A few of them now just ask directly, at dinner, in January: what are you seeing lately. The answers have funded renovations.

angles.drive: People warm to you before you finish your first sentence, and doors follow. The upgrade appears, the stranger extends the invitation, the gatekeeper finds an exception with your name on it. Charm this natural is not performed. It is a temperature, and everyone drifts toward it.
angles.cost_self: You walked into the fully booked restaurant behind two parties who had been turned away, and left with a corner table, the chef’s recommendation, and a standing invitation. Your dinner companion timed the whole ascent: four minutes. She has retold that timing at every gathering since.
angles.cost_others: Gatherings rearrange around your arrival, which you notice less than everyone else does. Hosts introduce you first, strangers remember your name, and follow-ups appear in your inbox from conversations you barely registered. The network effect is compounding. Other people network. You just show up warm.

angles.drive: Your speed between spark and action embarrasses whole planning departments. The idea from breakfast has a domain name by lunch and revenue by the quarter’s end. Momentum is your natural state, and hesitation, wherever you encounter it, reads to you as a foreign language.
angles.cost_self: The pop-up went from group-chat joke to opening night in nineteen days, permits included. People asked how long you had been planning it. The honest answer, since the joke, confused them into laughter. The line outside, though, was fluent in results.
angles.cost_others: Partners either learn your tempo or watch from the platform. By the time competitors finish their market analysis, you are iterating on version two with actual customer complaints, which you consider the only research with calories in it. The analysts eventually cite you. As data.

angles.drive: Every new shine gets your full sprint. The trend, the token, the just-opened thing: you arrive first, burn bright, and are gone before the substance question comes up. Chasing light is genuinely fun. A portfolio of chases, though, is mostly a photo album of exits.
angles.cost_self: You were early to the app everyone joined and earlier out, early to the seltzer brand, the course platform, the resale game. Each sprint made money for three months and stories forever. The friend who boringly stayed in one lane just bought a house. You have anecdotes.
angles.cost_others: People invite your read on what is next and quietly discount your staying power, a distinction that took you years to notice. The introductions still come. What stopped coming are the long-term seats, the ones reserved for people who will still be there when the shine dulls.

angles.drive: Money exits you at the speed of delight. The round for the table, the gadget of the month, the upgrade that felt like destiny at checkout: each purchase is warm and defensible, and together they are a bonfire with a loyalty card. Earning was never your problem. Keeping never got hired.
angles.cost_self: The bonus landed on the fourth and was structurally gone by the nineteenth: the trip booked, the jacket, the speakers, the generous gesture at dinner that felt so right. Nothing was wasted, exactly. Nothing was kept, either. The statement reads like a wonderful month someone else paid for.
angles.cost_others: Friends love going out with you and wince at your math. The generosity is legendary and the reserves are rumor. People close to you have started celebrating your windfalls nervously, knowing the celebration itself will consume a measurable percentage. Somebody gifted you a budgeting app once. You upgraded it to premium.

angles.drive: Your commitments have the lifespan of sparks. The plan ignites, glows, and is ash by the follow-through date, replaced by a newer, brighter plan in the same weekend. People stopped writing your intentions in ink around the time you did, which was never.
angles.cost_self: The Portugal trip was real for eleven days: researched, group-chatted, half-booked. Then the sailing course appeared, then the food truck idea, and by month’s end Portugal was a tab among tabs. Your browser history is an atlas of abandoned futures, each one sincerely meant for a week.
angles.cost_others: People triangulate your actual plans by waiting a month and checking what survived. Employers, partners, and one long-suffering travel agent have all developed the same policy: nothing books until you mention it a third time. You find the policy insulting. It has never once been wrong.

angles.drive: Money leaves your hands warm. The fair wage rounded up, the invoice paid the day it arrives, the tip that acknowledges the human: your dealings carry heat without waste, and people remember transacting with you the way they remember good meals, specifically and fondly.
angles.cost_self: You paid the young decorator his full quote the same evening, plus the amount his underquoting had cost him, with a note about knowing his worth. He kept the note. Three years and one thriving business later, he still bumps your jobs to the front of his book.
angles.cost_others: Tradespeople answer your calls first, sellers hold things for you unasked, and your name in a transaction thaws the terms. The premium you occasionally pay for decency keeps returning as priority, honesty, and first refusal. Your money makes friends everywhere it goes, and they all remember your address.

angles.drive: Your effort burns steady, on schedule, without applause requirements. The daily block, the maintained log, the follow-through that arrives exactly when promised: the work gets done at a sustainable temperature, every day, and the years quietly assemble the results into something substantial.
angles.cost_self: The certification took eighteen months of Tuesday and Thursday evenings, logged without drama while louder colleagues announced bootcamps they never finished. When the title bump came, people called it sudden. The logbook, four notebooks thick by then, had a different word for it.
angles.cost_others: Managers hand you the long-burn projects, the ones that die in flashier hands, because your fire does not need feeding by an audience. What you tend, finishes. The portfolio of finished things has become your entire argument, and it wins every review without your voice rising once.

angles.drive: Your word converts to certainty at full rate. The quote holds, the date holds, the handshake survives price movements: people budget on your commitments the way they budget on math. Being counted on is your asset class, and its yield compounds in reputation.
angles.cost_self: The contractor overran and your quote did not, absorbing the difference exactly as promised, exactly once. The client noticed both halves: the cost you ate and the silence you ate it with. Their next three projects arrived un-tendered, with a note: your number is the number.
angles.cost_others: Around you, people stop building backup plans. The backup plans for your deliverables have quietly disappeared from other people’s spreadsheets, which is the highest compliment operations can pay. New partners get told simply: whatever that one says will happen, price it as done.

angles.drive: The flame gets rationed like the last match. The heating negotiated by degrees, the gift budgeted to the occasion’s minimum, the generosity metered through a nozzle: nothing is ever quite wasted, and nothing is ever quite warm. The savings are real. So is the temperature.
angles.cost_self: The birthday gift was practical, correctly sized, and returned the following week for something the recipient actually wanted, an exchange conducted politely and remembered longer than the birthday. You noticed the return in the account. You did not mention it. Neither did they, at length.
angles.cost_others: People have quietly re-sorted you from ask to do not bother, and the re-sorting saved you money that cost you invitations. The rounds you never bought, the collections you queried, the split hairs at every bill: each small defense held. The territory it defended has emptied.

angles.drive: Money worry runs in you like a pilot light, never quite off. The balance gets checked at midnight, the small expense triggers the big spiral, and windfalls arrive pre-ruined by the question of losing them. The accounts are healthy. The relationship with them is not.
angles.cost_self: The unexpected dental bill was covered by any of four accounts, and still cost you a weekend of recalculating retirement projections at the kitchen table, again, with the door closed. Your partner watched the light under the door. The numbers were fine. The light stayed on till two.
angles.cost_others: People around you have learned that financial topics change your breathing, and they steer accordingly: trips proposed with cost worked out in advance, gifts disguised as luck. The care is loving and constant and slightly exhausting, and everyone maintains it because the alternative is watching you calculate.

angles.drive: Every risk gets triple-checked until it leaves. The opportunity waits while you verify, the verified thing waits while you re-verify, and the moment, which had a temperature, cools to safe and worthless. Nothing bad gets past you. The cost is everything that needed slight courage.
angles.cost_self: The franchise opportunity cleared your first review, your second, and your accountant’s, and died awaiting your third, taken instead by a former colleague with worse analysis and a signature. Their opening party invitation sat on your counter for a month. You checked their numbers annually, after.
angles.cost_others: People pitch you first for rigor and elsewhere for money, a routing everyone understands and nobody explains to you. Your due diligence is borrowed by half your circle, applied to deals you declined. The finder’s fees that never existed would, by now, have funded the caution.

angles.drive: Pressure is where your thinking gets clear. Since you need certainty more than comfort, you let outside pressure clear your head rather than make your own calm. Choose some of that pressure yourself, because you are only this clear with something at stake.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the pressure lifts, your clear head goes with it and a quiet week feels like punishment. You would rather be clear under pressure than at ease without it. Let one quiet week count as rest, because you trade the rest you need for clarity.
angles.cost_others: You bring pressure into calm places. Since you think more clearly under pressure, you put it on the people near you as much as yourself. Keep most of that pressure for yourself, because you take a calm evening from the people at home.

angles.drive: Taking charge comes to you before anyone offers it. Standing by while a group drifts feels worse than being wrong out loud, so you take charge ahead of the vote. Hand the next one over, because you take charge better by choice than by habit.
angles.cost_self: Being in charge weighs on you once you take it. You feel safer in charge alone than sharing it, so you are rarely carried. Let one person carry part of it, because you pay for being in charge by never being looked after.
angles.cost_others: Wherever a plan stalls, you take charge and mean it kindly. Because a slow group feels risky, you take charge rather than wait your turn. Leave the next one to them, since each time you take charge you take their chance to decide.

angles.drive: Nothing at stake feels to you like being passed over. Since you only come awake with something to lose, you take high stakes over sure things. Keep one high-stakes thing going, because you were built to be tested rather than kept safe.
angles.cost_self: Loving high stakes means a calm stretch never feels like a reward. You would rather raise the stakes on a sure thing than let it stay sure. Let something good keep its low stakes, because you spend the calm you could have had.
angles.cost_others: When a day has no stakes, you add some. Since an easy win bores you more than a hard loss, you raise everyone's stakes with yours. Keep high stakes for your own plans, because you take the plain good day from those beside you.

angles.drive: You are harder on yourself than anyone else has been. With Fire past what your strength holds, you would sooner be hard on yourself than let one mistake go. Remember that you never passed a test by going hard on yourself for failing it.
angles.cost_self: Long before anyone sees a mistake, you are already hard on yourself. No day off feels earned under that hardness, so you apologise for rest rather than take it. Bear in mind that being this hard on yourself costs you days off never taken.
angles.cost_others: Your hardness on yourself never stays private. Since you give yourself no pass, you hold those close to you to your standard rather than theirs. Remind yourself that being so hard on yourself in front of them takes the ease from their evening.

angles.drive: Your push arrives before anyone has asked for it. Because waiting for a yes feels like losing ground, you push people along ahead of asking whether they wanted pushing. Do not forget that you push a person as hard as you push a problem.
angles.cost_self: Each time you push too hard, you spend strength you do not have. You would rather push through than keep the energy to finish the week. You pay for pushing too hard in lost sleep, so remember that the bill is yours alone.
angles.cost_others: Pushing people toward an answer is faster than walking them there. Since you trust a push over patience, you push whoever is nearest whether they asked or not. Before the next push, remember that you are harder to be close to than to follow.

angles.drive: Going off duty is an order you never learned to take. Since you feel safe only with something to handle, you stay on duty ahead of ending the day. Remember you were made to meet a crisis rather than stay on duty after it.
angles.cost_self: When one emergency ends, you look for the next rather than go off duty. You never take a rest you did not fight for, so duty is your normal. Only you can call yourself off duty, and waiting costs you every evening at home.
angles.cost_others: Staying on duty is how you love the people in your care. Since being on duty comes easier than company, you give them a guard ahead of someone to sit with. Remember how hard you are to reach when most on duty for them.

angles.drive: Every promise you make becomes a rule you keep. Being relied on is the closest you get to feeling safe, so you keep your word ahead of your freedom to change it. Promise a little less freely, because you keep every one you make.
angles.cost_self: Keeping a promise costs you the right to change your mind. You would rather keep a stale promise than break it, so you stay inside plans past their use. Let yourself out of one, because you turn down better offers to keep old promises.
angles.cost_others: To you, a passing promise is one to keep. Because a promise is a rule rather than a wish, you hold everyone to every one they make. Let small promises go, since you leave your friends no freedom to have only been talking.

angles.drive: By the book is the only way you trust a thing done. Since an outside rule steadies you, you go by the book ahead of the shortcut. Stay with the book, because you are the standard the work gets checked against.
angles.cost_self: Where the book and your judgment part, you side with the book. You want it done in order more than your way, so you let the book decide what you knew. Allow the book one exception, because you give up chances that cannot wait.
angles.cost_others: Doing it by the book counts as respect paid forward. Because you want it right more than fast, you hold a friend's rushed job to the book too. Name the book out loud first, since you take the easy way from everyone beside you.

angles.drive: A fairly earned title is worth more to you than any praise. Since an earned rank says you belong, you earn the next title ahead of chasing the next thrill. Let the title come slowly, because you are already doing the job it names.
angles.cost_self: Earning the title comes first, claiming it long after. You want to look deserving more than to be paid, so you earn it twice before asking once. Claim it now, because earning it this slowly leaves money you were owed on the table.
angles.cost_others: Where titles are concerned, you make everyone earn theirs too. Since an unearned rank looks like cheating, you give a colleague the long route rather than a quiet word. Say the word sometimes, because you take from them the years that earning costs.

angles.drive: A rule you learned once stays in force after it stops helping. The rules that steady you also hold you in, until you keep the correct one ahead of the useful one. You wrote most of these rules yourself, and you can retire them.
angles.cost_self: Between a rule and a chance, you take the rule. You put being correct ahead of being free, so your career keeps the rules and never jumps. Bear in mind that you keep each rule at the price of jobs you never went for.
angles.cost_others: Keeping to the rules is how you look after people. Because one exception feels like a collapse starting, you give them the rule ahead of what they asked for. Never forget that you hand the rules holding you in to everyone living with you.

angles.drive: Fear of slipping runs under most of what you do well. Since your standing holds your worth, you would rather never be seen to slip than be at ease. Remember how much less you are watched for a slip than watching for one.
angles.cost_self: One slip stays with you longer than with anyone who saw it. Afraid to slip, you put looking steady ahead of feeling rested, until good days tire you like bad ones. Remind yourself how much rest you lose over slips you never made.
angles.cost_others: Hiding every slip is how you serve those who depend on you. Since a visible slip reads as failed duty, you offer them a composed self ahead of a true one. Before hiding the next slip, remember that you take their chance to help.

angles.drive: Every duty offered gets a yes before you check its cost. Since being counted on is where your standing lives, you never say no to the next request ahead of finishing the last. Remember you can only say yes for as long as you last.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you say yes, you spend hours promised to yourself. Because holding things together comes ahead of getting home, you trade sleep for another duty. You are nobody's standard once you run out of sleep to say yes with, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_others: Saying yes to everyone keeps your place in their lives. Because a refusal feels like lost standing, you give everyone a slice rather than anyone your whole self. You will want to remember that you give those who need you most whatever is left.

angles.drive: You see finished things where others see empty air. The business before the market exists, the picture before the first stroke, the version of a person they have not met yet. The visions arrive lit from inside, complete, and your job is mostly transcription.
angles.cost_self: You described the neighborhood’s future to a skeptical friend in 2019, cafe by cafe, almost address by address. You were renting there anyway when the wave arrived. The friend brings up that walk every time property prices come up, in the tone people use for eclipses.
angles.cost_others: People dismiss your predictions at intake and quote them at parties three years later. The pattern has repeated enough that a few colleagues now write down your stray remarks, timestamped, as a hobby. Their notebook, they say, outperforms their financial advisor. They are not entirely joking.

angles.drive: Your mind switches on when the world switches off. After eleven, the connections arrive: the insight, the fix, the strange idea with the workable center. Daylight-you executes what midnight-you discovers, a two-shift operation everyone mistakes for one ordinary person.
angles.cost_self: The solution to the storage problem arrived at 1:40am, complete, while the house slept, and you built the prototype by breakfast using a lamp and a towel to muffle the drill. The team spent Tuesday marveling. You spent Tuesday napping, having already been to Wednesday.
angles.cost_others: People learn to check their messages in the morning for your timestamps: 12:51, 2:14, 3:03, each carrying something the daylight meetings could not produce. Employers have stopped policing your hours. Whatever happens in your small hours arrives at standup already glowing, and nobody audits a lighthouse.

angles.drive: Your knowing arrives without visible sources. The diagnosis before the tests, the reading of a stranger at a glance, the sense that this flight, this deal, this person is wrong. Asked to explain, you produce nothing auditable. Asked to be right, you mostly are.
angles.cost_self: You told your friend not to take the apartment, unable to name a single concrete reason beyond the light felt wrong. She took it. The mold survey, the neighbor situation, and the landlord’s lawsuit all surfaced within the year, in roughly the order your discomfort had.
angles.cost_others: People consult you off the record, slightly embarrassed, the way executives consult weather folklore before big launches. Your hit rate embarrasses them further. Nobody builds a slide around your feelings, and increasingly nobody signs anything big without, casually, asking what your gut says first.

angles.drive: One idea takes the whole house. The new interest arrives like ignition: gear bought, sleep skipped, meals forgotten, conversation rerouted through the topic for weeks. The heat is genuine and total, and everything else in your life stands in its light, waiting, unwatered.
angles.cost_self: The chess phase lasted seven weeks and consumed roughly two hundred hours, four apps, one physical clock, and every anecdote you told. Then, on an unremarkable Thursday, it simply stopped burning. The board is under the bed now, with the telescope, the loom, and the kanji cards.
angles.cost_others: Your people track your obsessions like weather systems: naming them, estimating duration, planning around the blast radius. They have learned not to invest in the current one and not to mention the last one. What they miss, quietly, is the version of you between fires. He rarely visits.

angles.drive: Your energy arrives on a schedule no one, including you, can publish. Tuesday-you rewires the kitchen at midnight and Thursday-you cannot answer a text. Plans made in a bright phase get inherited by a dim one, and both phases sign your name with equal authority.
angles.cost_self: You committed to the weekend workshop during Monday’s blaze, prepaid and enthusiastic, and arrived at Saturday as a different person, one who sat in the parking lot for forty minutes and drove home. The refund window had closed. The pattern, your partner noted, has a subscription.
angles.cost_others: People quote two versions of you and specify which one they mean: bright-you and gone-you. Invitations come with soft confirmations layered in, checked twice, once at acceptance and once the night before. Nobody calls it unreliability to your face. The scheduling apparatus around you says it hourly.
